statement: The table shows some values of the function $f$. $$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline f(x) & 7 & 4 & 3 & 4 & 7 \end{array}$$ The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = 2f(x + 1) - 3$. What is the value of $g(1)$?

choices.misconception: I shifted the input the wrong way and used $f(1 - 1) = f(0) = 7$, so I computed $2(7) - 3$.
I ignored the $+1$ inside the function and used $f(1) = 4$, so I computed $2(4) - 3$.
I subtracted $3$ before doubling, so I computed $2(f(2) - 3) = 2(3 - 3)$.

hints: Start inside the parentheses: what input does $f$ receive when $x = 1$?
